In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

brand avoidance of Gen Z is driven by the following factors: (1) the fast fashion brands do not offer a unique product or service, (2) the brands are not authentic, (3) they do not have a strong social mission, (4) they do not offer a good value for money and (5) the brands are associated with unethical business practices.
Gen Z consumers are more likely to avoid fast fashion brands, if they are perceived to be low quality, low value, and low ethical brands.
the avoidance of fast fashion brands among Gen Z is mainly driven by the moral avoidance, followed by the identity avoidance, the experience avoidance and the advertising avoidance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brand avoidance behaviour is a multidimensional concept, which can be divided into five categories: experience avoidance, identity-avoidance, moral avoidance, value avoidance, and advertising avoidance.
the brand avoidance behaviour in case of Gen Z in the fast fashion industry is mainly driven by identity avoidance and moral avoidance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
fast fashion brands are not able to satisfy Gen Z's needs in a sustainable and ethical manner, and that they are perceived to be a threat for the environment and the society.
the avoidance of fast fashion brands is a multidimensional phenomenon, which cannot be reduced to a single factor.

the avoidance of fast fashion brands is not only related to the negative aspects of the brands themselves (e.g. unethical production, low quality, poor sustainability), but also to the negative aspects related to the consumers' identity, and the consumers' moral and social values.
